prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a hit while turning left in Sugar Land, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1069; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you were involved in while turning left in Sugar Land, Texas. Do you understand that this conversation is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Please state your full name and the best phone number to reach you.

A: I'd rather keep my personal details off the recording unless you really need them. You already have my policy information.

Q: That's fine. Can you describe what you were doing right before the collision?

A: I was driving home from the store. I came up to the intersection with the light green, and I wanted to turn left into the shopping center driveway.

Q: Did you have a turn signal on?

A: Yes, I put my signal on about a hundred feet before the intersection.

Q: What happened when you began your turn?

A: There was a car coming the other way. I thought it had stopped, so I started to go, and then it came through the intersection and hit the front corner of my car.

Q: Did you feel any injuries immediately after the impact?

A: Not right away. I was shaken up, but I thought I was okay. By that evening my neck was stiff and my lower back was sore, and it's gotten worse since.

Q: Have you sought medical treatment for those symptoms?

A: Yes, I went to urgent care the next morning. They diagnosed a neck strain and a back strain and gave me a referral to physical therapy.

Q: Are you still receiving treatment?

A: Yes, I have physical therapy twice a week, and I still have trouble sleeping because of the pain.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just want to get my car repaired and get back to normal.

Q: Thank you for your cooperation. This concludes the statement.
